c4-maths.q: Look at a ball from the top. What shape do you see?

c4-maths.q: 7 children want to dance in pairs. Will anyone be left without a partner?

c4-maths.q: 50, 45, 40, 35, ___. What comes next?

c4-maths.q: 100, 90, 80, ___, ___. What are the next two numbers?

c4-maths.q: Estimate: is a classroom door about 2 m tall or about 2 cm tall?

c4-maths.q: Eggs come in trays of 6. How many eggs are in 3 trays?

c4-maths.q: What is 6 × 0?

c4-maths.q: Compare 6 + 0 and 6 × 0. What does each give?

c4-maths.q: Work out 57 + 9 the quick way: add 10, then take away 1.

c4-maths.q: In the addition chart, 6 + 4 = 10. Name two other pairs that make 10.

c4-maths.q: Fold a paper heart down the middle. Do the two halves match exactly?

c4-evs.q: Explain to your little cousin Golu what three public places in your neighbourhood do for people.
c4-evs.why: Naming familiar public places and services is early neighbourhood learning.

c4-evs.q: Golu says: 'A neem tree is not a living thing. It can't walk and it doesn't eat.' Find the mistake.

c4-evs.q: Quick memory check: what is special about a duck's feet, and what do they help it do?

c4-evs.q: From last time: name one plant used for medicine and one used to build a house.

c4-evs.q: Give one food for each taste: sweet, salty, sour, bitter.

c4-evs.q: Name four feelings people can have.

c4-evs.q: From last time: what happens at the chakki?

c4-evs.q: From last time: why do houses in places with heavy rain or snow have sloping roofs?
c4-evs.why: Single familiar recall: sloping roofs let precipitation slide off.

c4-evs.q: From last time: what is a shadow, in one line?
c4-evs.why: Only asks a simple, familiar definition of a shadow.

c4-english.why: Identifying whether two spoken words rhyme is an early literacy skill.

c4-english.q: In our poem, what do many raindrops make?
c4-english.why: Single factual recall using very simple vocabulary.

c4-english.q: Riya cannot lift a heavy box of books alone. Three friends come to help her. What will happen next?
c4-english.why: Outcome is obvious from an everyday teamwork situation.

c4-english.q: Fill in the gap: 'A ___ of sticks is hard to break.' Is it 'bundle' or 'bubble'?
c4-english.why: Picture-book vocabulary with only two highly distinct choices.

c4-english.q: What is the English word for 'saath milkar'?
c4-english.why: Asks one common English translation as direct recall.

c4-english.q: Make your own sentence with the word 'together'.
c4-english.why: Creating a basic sentence with a familiar word is elementary.

c4-english.q: Complete with 'can' or 'can't': 'One raindrop ___ fill a pot.'
c4-english.why: Simple everyday reasoning plus a binary word choice.

c4-english.why: Footpath use is elementary road-safety knowledge.

c4-english.q: What does a red traffic light mean?
c4-english.why: Traffic-light meaning is a widely known everyday fact.

c4-english.why: Recalls a familiar road-crossing routine in three short steps.

c4-english.q: What is the English word for the 'topi' you wear on a scooter to protect your head?
c4-english.why: Asks for one common everyday safety word.

c4-english.q: What is the difference between a 'footpath' and a 'road'?
c4-english.why: Distinguishes two familiar places using their basic purposes.

c4-english.q: Why is it called a 'zebra' crossing?
c4-english.why: Recognises the obvious visual similarity of black-and-white stripes.

c4-english.why: Applies a basic safety rule to an obvious danger.

c4-english.why: Correcting a to an before a vowel is elementary grammar.

c4-english.q: How old was Louis when he hurt his eye?
c4-english.why: Single factual recall requiring no explanation or reasoning.

c4-english.q: How do people who cannot see read Braille?

c4-english.q: What is the Hindi meaning of 'blind'?
c4-english.why: Direct translation of a common basic English word.

c4-english.why: Demonstrating or explaining a common action needs only basic vocabulary.

c4-english.q: What is the difference between 'skip' and 'jump'?
c4-english.why: Distinguishes two familiar physical actions using everyday vocabulary.

c4-english.why: Requires recalling only one explicitly stated word from the play.

c4-english.why: Asks direct recall of one explicitly taught expression.

c4-english.q: What is the difference between a 'tale' and a 'tail'?
c4-english.why: Distinguishing common homophones requires only basic vocabulary.

c4-english.q: Find the mistake: 'Two tiger stepped into the circle.'
c4-english.why: Correcting a regular plural after two is elementary grammar.

c4-english.q: Listen: 'Up I go, up to the sky, / Higher than the birds can ___!' Which word fits?

c4-english.q: Find the word that rhymes with 'sway' in the poem.
c4-english.why: Identifying one rhyming word is an early-primary poetry skill.

c4-english.q: What rushes past the child when the swing comes down?
c4-english.why: Requires recalling one explicitly stated detail from the poem.

c4-english.q: What is the opposite of 'up'? And of 'back' in 'back and forth'?
c4-english.why: Tests two elementary opposites commonly learned in Class 1.

c4-english.why: It requires recalling one explicitly named means of transport.

c4-english.why: The supplied place answer directly cues the basic word where.

c4-english.why: Requires only direct recall of the immediately following event.

c4-hindi.q: In the poem, what was the bird's very first home like?
c4-hindi.why: Requires only one simple, explicitly stated detail.

c4-hindi.q: Then her home became a nest. What was the nest made of?
c4-hindi.why: Asks for one concrete detail directly stated in the poem.

c4-hindi.q: When the bird says the world is ‘इतना-सा’, does she mean very small or very big?
c4-hindi.why: Identifying इतना-सा as small is basic vocabulary comprehension.

c4-hindi.q: Flying far across the sky, what did the bird finally understand?

c4-hindi.why: Forms a common singular-to-plural noun change.

c4-hindi.q: Say a new word, not in the poem, that rhymes with गाता.
c4-hindi.why: एक सरल तुकांत शब्द बताना प्रारंभिक भाषा-कौशल है।

c4-hindi.q: Fill in: नीम की पत्ती ___ होती है (कड़वा / कड़वी).
c4-hindi.why: सामान्य संज्ञा-विशेषण लिंग-सामंजस्य चुनना है।

c4-hindi.q: According to the poem, eating rice, dal and vegetables brings what into the body?
c4-hindi.why: Only recalls one explicitly stated phrase from the poem.

c4-hindi.q: The poem says don't bring only potatoes. Which other vegetables does it name? Say any two.
c4-hindi.why: कविता से दो सब्ज़ियों के नाम सीधे दोहराने हैं।

c4-hindi.q: Which fruits and vegetables take away the pain of summer heat in the poem? Say any two.
c4-hindi.why: पंक्ति से दो परिचित खाद्य नाम पहचानने हैं।

c4-hindi.q: In the poem, which word rhymes with खीरा?
c4-hindi.why: कविता में दिया एक तुकांत शब्द खोजना है।

c4-hindi.q: In the poem खाओ rhymes with लाओ. Say two new words that rhyme with खाओ.
c4-hindi.why: दो सामान्य ‘आओ’ तुकांत शब्द बनाने हैं।

c4-hindi.q: What does आहार mean?

c4-hindi.q: Find all the naming words in: ‘मीना ने थाली में रोटी और दाल रखी।’

c4-hindi.q: While running, whom did the rabbit meet first — the bear, the fox or the elephant?
c4-hindi.why: तीन विकल्पों में कहानी का सीधा क्रम याद करना है।

c4-hindi.q: Fill in: ‘लोमड़ी भी भागने ___।’ (लगा / लगी)

c4-hindi.q: I wrote: ‘जंगल में एक सेर रहता था।’ Catch the spelling mistake.

c4-hindi.why: पत्र से स्थान और प्राप्तकर्ता की सीधी पहचान है।

c4-hindi.q: Amar says they are going to Udaipur, the ‘city of lakes’. Guess why it might be called that.
c4-hindi.why: उपनाम से बहुत सीधा, एक-कदम अनुमान लगाना है।
